newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares enlivened by good news from U.S.
newsitem.headline: German shares enlivened by good news from U.S.

text.p: Softer-than-expected U.S. data drove German shares sharply higher in afternoon trade on Tuesday as a mini-rally by Bunds buoyed interest in the banking and insurance sector.

The 30-share IBIS DAX index soared after the release of U.S. employment costs and durable goods orders data, breaching a key resistance level at 3,400 points to trade up 50.86 points at 3,423.82 points at 1308 GMT, 40 points above the mid-afternoon bourse closing level.
"Things are certainly positive in the very short term but I wouldn"t see this as real euphoria," cautioned one trader.

"With the public holiday just around the corner (May Day on Thursday) I can see some people flattening out their positions before too long. And there hasn't been enough of a broad sweep ahead to convince me," the trader added.
Banks and insurance companies, which often outperform when bond markets are strong because of the large fixed income portfolios they control, were among the leaders.
Insurer Allianz AG Holding was up 4.21 percent at 334.50 marks in afternoon trade while Deutsche Bank AG was up 1.33 marks at 89.70 marks, broadly in line but amid heavy trading volumes.
Bayerische Vereinsbank AG was up 1.68 marks, or 2.5 percent, at 68.50 marks.

Engineering giant Siemens AG also continued its surge on the back of what dealers said were technical buy signals. Its shares were the heaviest traded of the day and were up 2.30 marks, or 2.54 percent, at 92.75 marks in afternoon trade.
Chemicals group Degussa AG, however, defied the market trend by easing in response to the release of first half earnings in the morning, which dealers said had had a mixed reception.
Degussa reported first-half sales of 7.2 billion marks and a 25 percent profit rise to 233 million marks.
"It was partly a case of 'sell on good news'," said one Frankfurt trader.

Dealers also said that Degussa's profit exceeded many expectations but that sales were at the lower end of forecasts. Its shares were down 1.60 marks, or two percent at 78.40 marks -- making it the weakest blue chip stock of the day.
Dealers said they would look to Wall Street for their next signal, with a sharp reaction to the U.S. data expected.
